Hi Samira —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for the private deployment. Attached is a concise onboarding checklist and a short mutual action plan (MA plan) to help structure the account wiring and environment validation. High-level asks to kick things off:

- Confirm target VPC CIDR(s) and whether you prefer a dedicated tenant VPC or a peered/shared model.
- Provide point-of-contact for KMS/HSM and whether keys will be in your KMS or managed by Redwood.
- Confirm egress policy: will outbound to S3/OSS be routed through a NAT or through a controlled proxy?
- Any procurement or SSO requirements we should include in the SOW/DPA?

3) Egress: minimal outbound allowed — all S3 traffic must go through our egress proxy.
4) Compliance: we need a short list of artifacts for SOC 2 evidence (audit logs, network ACL changes, KMS access audit).

Samira —

Thanks for the diagram and questions. Quick answers and action items from the infra side:

- Dedicated tenant VPC: recommended for strict isolation. If you need cross-environment communication, we usually recommend a transit VPC pattern with strict route filtering; we can include a reference topology in the runbook.
- KMS integration: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS. We never export plaintext keys; we use envelope encryption. We’ll need the KMS key ARN(s) and a policy that allows our service role to Encrypt/Decrypt as needed for tokenization and cache persistence.
- Egress proxy: we can pin outbound S3 and telemetry to your proxy. Please share proxy FQDNs and TLS cert expectations.
- SOC 2 artifacts: we will prepare an evidence pack (audit logs, access change history, network ACL change list) — expect a short checklist from us ahead of the kickoff.

Open asks for your team before the preflight:
- CIDR ranges for prod/preprod/staging
- KMS key ARN(s) and admin contact
- List of IPs/subnets allowed for bastion and engineer jump boxes (we recommend single egress NAT for outbound).

I’m attaching our network egress policy template for your security team to review.

Attachments: redwood-network-egress-policy-template.yaml

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Deployment Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Novacare private footprint readiness: preflight & account wiring checklist

Samira / team —

A few technical specifics we’ll want locked prior to day-0 activation:

- Required ports: 443 outbound (for model pulls/telemetry), 22 inbound only to bastion (if SSH is used) and JMAP 10250 (internal health) — we’ll provide a minimal ports matrix in the runbook.
- KV cache persistence: if you expect warm-started long context workloads, we recommend an EBS-backed KV cache snapshot mechanism. Confirm whether snapshots will be stored in your S3 bucket (we’ll need write policy).
- DNS & hostnames: provide the FQDNs you’d like for the control-plane endpoints. If you prefer internal-only, we’ll issue certs against those names and provide CSR instructions.
- NAT vs. egress gateway: if all outbound must go through your proxy, we’ll route traffic through it and disable public egress from the tenant. Confirm proxy endpoints and whether mTLS is required.

I uploaded a skeleton runbook with the preflight checklist and example firewall rules to the shared Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bNovacareOnboardRunbook. Please drop the CIDRs and cert contacts into the Runbook doc.
